search_bias: evaluation/verifiers; measurement validity; paired anytime-valid acceptance, nuisance-discordance adaptation, and finite-horizon power

public_sources.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
public_sources.used_scope: Direct agent application of a paired discordant-outcome betting e-process. Default alpha=0.05, lambda=0.5. The theorem is per candidate conditional on its evaluation stream, not a run-level familywise guarantee; the paper explicitly treats loop-level adaptive reuse of the dev set as empirical rather than a theoretical claim. Demonstrated only for prompt-level Qwen2.5 agents on GSM8K, SVAMP and ARC-Challenge.

public_sources.title: E-values for k-Sample Tests with Exponential Families
public_sources.authors: Yunda Hao; Peter Grünwald; Tyron Lardy; Long Long; Reuben Adams
public_sources.used_scope: For k=2 Bernoulli blocks, conditioning on the pair sum makes concordant outcomes e-factor 1; sequential block e-variables can be multiplied for optional-stopping-safe tests. Composite alternatives can be handled by mixtures or plug-in methods. Used only to support the general conditioning/mixture design principle, not the worker-local finite-horizon optimization.

pace_parameter_translation.sign_bet_form: factor = 2a for candidate-only win; 2(1-a) for incumbent-only win; 1 for concordance
pace_parameter_translation.implication: PACE's default is exactly a fixed q=0.75 directional sign bet. Its anytime validity follows from the conditional sign null, but fixed a need not be finite-horizon or schedule-robust power-optimal.

posterior_rho_mixture_projection.setup: Fixed total-task horizon T=50, terminal one-sided exact McNemar rejection geometry. A reference model is used only to choose the predictable sign bet; null validity remains sign-only and therefore does not require the reference discordance model to be correct.
posterior_rho_mixture_projection.posterior: For history with t tasks and d discordances, posterior weight for fixed rho is proportional to prior(rho)*rho^d*(1-rho)^(t-d).
posterior_rho_mixture_projection.bet: For the next discordant sign, combine reference continuation values with posterior*rho weights, then set a = weighted_H_plus / weighted_(H_plus+H_minus). Because a is predictable, factor 2a/2(1-a)/1 remains a conditional e-variable under any actual predictable discordance schedule satisfying sign symmetry.
posterior_rho_mixture_projection.priors_tested: uniform, center-heavy, extreme-heavy, low-rho-heavy, high-rho-heavy, plus power-law low-rho priors proportional to (1-rho)^gamma.
posterior_rho_mixture_projection.scope: Worker-local derivation/simulation. This is not a published theorem of PACE or Hao et al.; only the one-step sign-e validity is analytic.

actual_discordance_schedules.ahead_high: predictable: rho=0.7 when cumulative discordant sign lead >=0, else 0.1
actual_discordance_schedules.ahead_low: predictable: rho=0.1 when cumulative discordant sign lead >=0, else 0.7

policies.mix_lowpow4: posterior rho-mixture, prior weights proportional to (1-rho)^4
policies.mix_lowpow6: posterior rho-mixture, prior weights proportional to (1-rho)^6

interpretation: The fixed PACE default is powerful when discordances are plentiful but is highly brittle in the ahead_low schedule: reject-by-50 is about 1.4%, versus 12.0-12.6% for the low-rho posterior mixtures and 14.2% for an extreme static rho_ref=0.1.

Pure maximin across these seven schedules favors rho_ref=0.1 (about 14.2% worst-case) but its average reject rate is only about 37.2%. A posterior mixture with low-rho prior is a better robustness/typical-power compromise: gamma=4 gives about 12.0% worst-case and 51.2% average; gamma=6 gives about 12.6% worst-case and 50.1% average.
A rho_ref tuned to common rho=0.4 has the highest average among the selected policies (about 53.4%) but only about 3.8% worst-case, exposing strong nuisance-schedule mismatch.

All selected sign e-processes had maximum empirical null crossing below 0.05 in the 250k-rep sanity checks, including outcome-adaptive schedules; this is consistent with, but is not a substitute for, the analytic one-step martingale argument.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use identical evaluation instances for incumbent/candidate, discard concordant binary pairs, multiply a sign betting e-process over discordances, and accept only at E>=1/alpha.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: PACE primary preprint reports 30-42% false and 10-33% harmful greedy commits in controlled prompt-evolution experiments, versus 0/5 audit-labelled false commits for PACE, ~18% lower evaluation cost, and strong churn suppression in stochastic experiments.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Prompt-level Qwen2.5 0.5B-3B on GSM8K/SVAMP/ARC; 3-5 seeds; audit labels are finite-sample measurements. The guarantee is per candidate conditional on its evaluation stream, not loop-level FWER/FDR. System-level transfer is argued, not demonstrated.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Use a posterior mixture over possible discordance rates only to choose the finite-horizon directional sign bet; keep e-validity anchored to predictable sign factors so actual rho may be misspecified or outcome-adaptive.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local 250k-rep/schedule simulations at T=50, q=0.75 show low-rho posterior mixtures materially reduce schedule brittleness relative to PACE's fixed lambda=0.5 and to a single rho_ref tuned for typical conditions.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Simulation model only; binary paired outcomes, one-sided sign null, T=50, specific rho schedules and q=0.75. No claim of universal optimality.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Choose reference-rho prior by explicit decision utility (maximin, average power, or weighted deployment prior), rather than labeling one finite-horizon betting policy globally optimal.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: In the same seven-schedule stress test, static rho_ref=0.1 maximizes observed worst-case rejection but loses large average power; rho_ref=0.4 maximizes selected average but collapses under low-when-ahead adaptation; low-rho mixtures occupy the middle Pareto region.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: The schedule set is a stress-test family, not a deployment distribution. Utility weights must be predeclared or separately justified.

measurement_validity_rules.rule_1: Separate anytime validity from power robustness: a fixed betting fraction can remain exactly valid yet have near-zero resolution under plausible adaptive discordance schedules.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_2: For paired agent acceptance, report the conditional sign-null assumption explicitly. 'McNemar-style' pairing alone does not establish loop-level validity when candidate generation and dev-set reuse are adaptive.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_3: Per-candidate false-commit control is not run-level familywise/FDR control. Report which guarantee is actually claimed.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_4: When a nuisance model is used only for bet selection, validate by the true one-step filtration identity and stress-test nuisance mismatch separately.
measurement_validity_rules.rule_5: Select finite-horizon betting/reference policies against an explicit utility or deployment prior; do not infer universal superiority from one rho/q/horizon.

frontier_queue.action: Analyze finite reused-dev-set validity for PACE-style gates when candidates are generated adaptively from the same D across rounds. Determine conditions under which the within-candidate conditional sign null remains defensible, and distinguish optional stopping within a candidate from adaptive data reuse across candidates.

Derive a continuous/Beta prior rho-mixture projection and optimize prior hyperparameters under explicit maximin versus Bayes-weighted utilities; compare to static rho_ref, PACE fixed lambda, and prior Bellman results across T=10,20,30,50.

Generalize the directional projection to uncertain/varying sign effect q and to two-sided superiority/noninferiority gates; include boundary randomization/discreteness handling where exact terminal tests leave alpha slack.

Search online-FWER/FDR/e-value allocation methods suitable for repeated candidate commits, while preserving the per-candidate paired e-process and without conflating run-level control with within-candidate optional stopping.

exact_next_action: Investigate the reused finite dev-set / adaptive-candidate-generation gap exposed explicitly by PACE: formalize when Pr(w_i=1 | within-candidate history)<=1/2 still follows after D has already steered earlier candidate generation, then compare remedies such as fresh audit data, reusable-holdout mechanisms, or run-level e-value allocation without sacrificing paired anytime-valid stopping.
